summary: @onereach/ui-components-common ships obfuscated preinstall dropper that fetches Bun runtime to execute opaque bundled payload
details: The package declares a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that runs on `npm install`. setup.mjs is obfuscated with obfuscator.io-style `_0xNNNN` identifier mangling and per-function string dictionaries containing tokens like `ldd`, `/etc/os-release`, `Alpine`, `powershell`, `-ExecutionPolicy`, and `Expand-Archive` — indicating cross-platform (Linux/Alpine/Windows) environment detection. It downloads the Bun runtime from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/...`, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and then `execFileSync`s Bun against a sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727 KB single-line Bun-compiled bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) with a scrambled string-array constant pool, a rotation function that permutes the array, and a custom alphabet-remap decoder — its behavior cannot be inspected without executing the decoder. `math_init.js` is not listed in package.json `files` (`["dist","src","./shims.d.ts","./tsconfig.components.json"]`) yet ships in the tarball root. The advertised purpose is a Vue UI-components library, which has no legitimate need to fetch a second language runtime at install time solely to execute a bundled opaque script. The alternate-runtime choice bypasses Node-based install-time scanners; the obfuscation on both the loader and the payload conceals the ultimate behavior. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern executing arbitrary attacker-controlled code on the installer's machine at `npm install` time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
